findings.reason: Proof step 1.1 asserts that the canonical shift is measurable but cites only the measure-preserving definition. Add the cylinder-preimage argument showing that inverse images of product cylinders are measurable.

The AMS proof does not establish that the Cesàro limit is stationary, although several consumers use this as a fact about the stationary mean. Add the telescoping calculation: the difference of the two averages is (P(T^{-N}E)-P(E))/N, which tends to zero.

The proof asserts 0 <= H_n <= n log2|A| without establishing the finite-alphabet entropy bound. Prove it against the uniform law on A^n, using lem-finite-kl-nonnegative-choice-free, and make that supplier use explicit.

The block-error code definition gives no encoder/decoder domains or message-set size cap for a rate-R code. lem-aep-implies-fixed-rate-lossless-coding assumes a cap of 2^floor(nR) without support from this definition. Specify the message set, maps, and rate cap, and prove that successful source blocks inject into the message set.
R_n is defined only for n >= 1, but L_W uses R_0. Define L_W as max({0} union {n >= 1: R_n <= W}), or explicitly define R_0, while preserving the stated empty-match convention.

The Statement covers finite measure-preserving systems, but the proof's Given clause restricts to a probability system and uses expectation notation. Align the proof hypotheses and integral notation with the full finite-measure scope.
The Proof's Given clause cites conventions [F1]-[F2], but only [F1] is defined. Step 1.1 uses the bit-log convention; add the missing finite-block information fact.

The proof establishes the entropy-rate limit by subadditivity but omits the Statement's claim that it equals the limit of finite-past conditional entropies. Use conditioning monotonicity, the chain rule and stationarity to write H_n as the sum of the first n finite-past conditional entropies, then apply Cesàro convergence.

Step 3 applies the displayed reverse-Fatou inequality to E_n^c, which does not yield the claimed bound for E_n. Derive the reverse-Fatou consequence by applying the actual Fatou supplier to 1_{E_n^c}, or apply the resulting inequality directly to E_n.
